items.headline: CENTCOM strikes Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz; Iran vows retaliation
items.summary: US forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday after IRGC forces were observed preparing to fire rockets and lay sea mines in the strait -- the first US military action against Iran in over a month, confirmed on record by CENTCOM spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins and independently corroborated by CNN, CNBC and Al Jazeera. Iran's IRGC publicly acknowledged the strike and vowed retaliation, calling it a "strategic and fatal mistake." A separate, single-sourced (Fox News, one unnamed US official) claim that Iran already retaliated against US forces in Jordan is UNCONFIRMED as of this run -- no CENTCOM, Pentagon, or wire-service (Reuters/AP) corroboration was found, and it is not treated as fact here.
items.actionable: A genuine military escalation (first confirmed US strike on Iran in weeks), not just sanctions rhetoric -- expect a haven bid in gold/silver and elevated volatility across the levered miners sleeve into Monday's Asia open, offsetting some of Friday's Warsh-driven rout; treat the Jordan-retaliation claim as unverified, not a basis for action.

items.headline: Oil jumps over 2% at the week's open on the Larak Island strike -- Brent back above $90, WTI near $85.41
items.summary: Brent crude climbed 2.52% to $90.32/bbl and WTI rose 2.41% to $85.41/bbl following the confirmed US strike on Iranian launchers -- corroborating our own price feed's Sunday-evening futures-reopen readings (WTI +1.77%, Brent +0.55%) with a real, sourced catalyst rather than routine drift. CENTCOM also said it has redirected 83 commercial vessels and disabled three others enforcing an Iranian-port blockade, with oil still crossing the blockade line at roughly 6.7m bbl/day per TankerTrackers data.
items.actionable: Rising energy prices reinforce the inflation/rate-hike narrative that hit precious metals Friday -- a genuine two-way pull on the miners sleeve: geopolitical haven demand up, but hawkish-Fed real-yield pressure also up.

items.headline: September Fed hike odds harden into a genuine coin-flip on CME and Kalshi
items.summary: CME FedWatch shows September hike odds at roughly 55.7%, about 20 points higher than pre-Warsh levels, while Kalshi prices a 47% hike / 54% hold split. The 2-year Treasury yield has moved up 12bp to 4.35% since Friday's speech -- the biggest jump since Warsh's first hawkish press conference in June.
items.actionable: The hike debate is no longer speculative -- it's a real 50/50 market-pricing event into the 16 Sep FOMC; size any silver/miner leverage additions with that binary risk explicitly in mind.

items.headline: Sanctioned UAE bank Banque Misr says it is 'reviewing' Treasury's notice; ~$1.8bn in flagged flows detailed
items.summary: Treasury's Friday action against Banque Misr's UAE branches (Operation Economic Outcast) is now detailed as targeting roughly $1.8bn processed over two years for ~100 companies allegedly tied to Iran's shadow banking network. Egypt's second-largest bank said Saturday it is reviewing the notice; only its UAE branches, not Egypt operations, lose US dollar/financial-system access.
items.actionable: Confirms the Iran sanctions campaign is being executed at real financial scale, not just rhetoric -- supportive of the broader Iran-risk-premium thesis already priced into gold; no direct portfolio action implied.

items.headline: Silver miners' August rally still outpaces the metal itself despite Friday's Warsh-driven rout
items.summary: Even after Friday's selloff, Hecla Mining is up 47% for August, First Majestic Silver +42%, and Pan American Silver +22% -- all ahead of silver's own monthly gain. The Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit for 2026, widening to 46.3m oz, on solar, EV and AI-infrastructure demand.
items.actionable: The structural deficit thesis behind the levered silver/miners sleeve is intact and the monthly trend remains strongly positive despite Friday's single-day shock -- treat Friday as noise within a still-bullish month rather than a trend break.

items.headline: JPMorgan downgrades OCBC to underweight, cuts DBS price target to S$63 from S$70
items.summary: JPMorgan downgraded OCBC to underweight (target cut to S$20.50) and lowered DBS's target to S$63 from S$70, while raising SGX's target -- citing asset-quality and geopolitical-risk concerns for the Singapore banking sector, a notable divergence from the sector's record 1H26 income prints.
items.actionable: A direct, negative read on two core portfolio holdings from a major house -- worth weighing against the banks' still-strong 1H26 income and margin data before adding to DBS/OCBC exposure.

items.headline: DBS Research reiterates Buy on Singtel, TP S$5.46, on Optus margin-expansion catalyst
items.summary: DBS maintains a Buy call on Singtel with an unchanged S$5.46 target, flagging management's internal target of OpCo EBIT reaching S$2.1-2.5bn by FY30, driven largely by Optus -- whose EBIT is expected to nearly double from S$488m (FY26) to roughly S$1.0bn by FY30.
items.actionable: A constructive multi-year read on Singtel's largest subsidiary supports the SGX sleeve's income thesis, independent of this weekend's Iran/Fed volatility.

items.headline: SMIC's interim report beats -- revenue +23.1% YoY, net profit +39.8%; shares jump 17.45% (A-share), 10.76% (HK)
items.summary: SMIC's 2026 interim report showed revenue up 23.1% YoY to RMB32.35bn and net profit up 39.8% to RMB2.3bn. The stock rallied 17.45% on the Shanghai market and 10.76% in Hong Kong on the print, pushing total market cap to roughly RMB578.2bn.
items.actionable: A strong fundamental beat for a direct portfolio holding -- the rally has largely already played out by Friday's close, so this is confirmation of the thesis rather than a fresh entry signal.

items.headline: China unveils property-sector reforms: 40-year mortgages, developer fundraising support, pre-sale escrow standards
items.summary: China's central bank will allow mortgages of up to 40 years (from 30), and the CSRC will support developer fundraising via equity and bond sales; new rules also require minimal upfront deposits and let buyers cancel if construction deadlines are missed. The reforms come as consumer spending has slowed and home prices kept falling.
items.actionable: A genuine policy-easing step for China's property sector and broader consumer sentiment -- modestly supportive of the China-risk-appetite backdrop for the HK tech sleeve, though it also underscores how weak underlying property demand still is.

items.headline: August set to be first month Ether ETF inflows overtake Bitcoin's; BTC ETFs end 9-day inflow streak with $202M outflow
items.summary: US spot Ether ETFs pulled in $3.87bn in August versus roughly $750m in net Bitcoin ETF outflows for the month -- the first time this has happened. Bitcoin ETFs still logged $924.5m over 24-28 Aug before a $202m outflow on Friday ended a nine-day, $3.04bn inflow streak, while Ether ETFs extended their own inflow streak to 10 straight sessions.
items.actionable: A genuine rotation signal within crypto (ETH over BTC) rather than a broad risk-off move -- Bitcoin itself is consolidating near $77-78k rather than breaking down, consistent with a rate-sensitive but not panicked market into Monday.

items.headline: Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut lifts September hike odds, 2yr yield and dollar (context for the weekend's harder-fought debate above)
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech ("In Our Time") said inflation is "still too high," explicitly declined to offer forward guidance, and floated cutting FOMC meetings from 8 to 6 a year. CME-tracked September hike odds jumped from ~36% to ~57-58% within the session, the 2-year Treasury yield rose 11.8bp to 4.348%, and the dollar index gained 0.5%.
items.actionable: The root cause of Friday's precious-metals rout and this weekend's hardened hike debate -- kept here as anchor context for the sleeve's largest near-term risk into the 16 Sep FOMC.
